Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 711 of 2023
Applicant :- Ram Sanehi
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. / Addl. Chief Secy.

Home Civil Secrett Counsel for Applicant :- Ashutosh Pratap Singh,Kunwar Bahadur Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J. 
Learned AGA informs that he has procured complete instructions in the matter including upto date case diary.
Thus, in the considered opinion of this Court, the anticipatory bail application moved on behalf of the applicant could be finally disposed of.
Heard Shri Ashutosh Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The present anticipatory bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Ram Sanehi in FIR No. 020/2021, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B, 409 IPC and 3/7 E.C. Act, Police Station Khodare, District Gonda, with the prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail as he is apprehending arrest in the above-mentioned case.

Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that it is a case of false implication and only on account of political enmity the instant FIR has been lodged wherein the allegation has been levelled to the tune that co-accused Shah Ali who is a licensee of fair price shop has not distributed the food grains to the eligible persons and the allegations against the Ram Sanehi vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. / Addl. ... on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169812743/
1 instant applicant are to the tune that he being the Pradhan of the village in connivance with Kotedar has certified the distribution which has not been disbursed by the Kotedar.
Highlighting the above fact, it is vehemently submitted that the function of the Pradhan in certifying the fair distribution was only based on the documents which were produced by the Kotedar before the applicant and the applicant was not aware as to whether any manipulation has been done by the Kotedar in the documents and the certificate of fair distribution was given in good faith as the duty of the applicant was not to remain present all the time at the fair price shop to assess the fair distribution and thus, no offence is emerging against the applicant, however, the Investigating Officer has submitted the charge sheet against the applicant also.

sentences.text: However, during the course of investigation in lieu of the order dated 26.3.2021 passed by a Division Bench of this Court in Writ Petition (M/B) No. 9409/2021, the protection from arrest was granted till submission of police report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C., applicant was not arrested.

It is also submitted that Kotedar who is an accused of not distributing the necessary items including the food grains to the card holders, has been granted anticipatory bail by a Coordinate Bench of this Court, vide order dated 27.2.2023 passed in CRIMINAL MISC ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION U/S 438 CR.P.C. No. - 497 of 2023.
The criminal history of one case has been adequately explained by the applicant and the case is not having any bearing on the instant case.
Thus, protection from arrest be granted to the instant applicant.
Learned AGA on the other hand submits that the applicant is an accused of committing heinous offence and therefore he is not entitled for any protection.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that the applicant was not arrested during the course of investigation and the charge sheet has been filed without arresting him and protection was granted under the orders of the Division Bench of this Court till submission of police report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C..

The applicant was the 'Pradhan'
of the village at relevant point of time and his work was of supervisory nature in authenticating distribution of food grains by Kotedar, while actual work of disbursing fairly was entrusted to the Kotedar, Shah Ali who has already been granted anticipatory bail from this Court.
The criminal history of one case has been explained adequately.

Thus, having regard to all the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra (2011) 1 SCC 694, Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia vs. State of Punjab [(1980) 2 SCC 565 : 1980 SCC (Cri)
561] as well as in Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) (2020) 5 SCC 1 and in Nathu Singh Vs State of U.P. and Others, 2021(6) SCC 64, MANU/SC/0360/2021, protection from arrest may be granted to the applicant during the course of trial as the charge sheet has already been submitted.

two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer/ SHO/ Investigating Officer/ trial court concerned, subject to the following conditions:
1. The applicant shall not leave India during the pendency of trial without prior permission from the concerned trial Court.
2. The applicant shall Cooperate in the investigation and will make himself available as and when required by the Investigating officer of the case, even for the recovery of any fact.
3. The applicant shall not make any attempt to influence the prosecution witnesses and will also not commit any crime during his release on anticipatory bail.
4. The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence and when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of any of above conditions, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law to ensure presence of the applicant.
5. In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail, the trial Court concerned may take appropriate action in accordance with law.

6. The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
If in the opinion of the trial court default of this condition is deliberate or without sufficient cause,
then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of his bail and shall proceed against him in accordance with law.
It is clarified that all the observations contained in this order are only for disposal of this anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial proceedings in any manner.
Order Date :- 22.3.2023
